title: 97 untouched Duck Hunt and Super Mario Bros. cartridges worth thousands discovered in retro shop storage room never-before-seen version of popular NES games include five perfect 10 PSA items
summary: A retro gaming shop in Wisconsin discovered a box of unopened NES cartridges, including 97 untouched Duck Hunt and Super Mario Bros. games worth thousands, with three items going up for auction starting August 12.
insight: Rarity and condition make these vintage games extremely valuable and sought-after.

title: Big tech spends more than $1 trillion on AI infrastructure additional $745 billion expected to be added to the figure in 2026 alone
summary: Big tech companies have spent over $1 trillion on AI investments since 2023, with an additional $745 billion expected in 2026. Their planned AI expenditures are set to increase, despite growing hidden debt of over $1.65 trillion. This trend highlights the significance of AI in the tech industry.
insight: Billions in AI investments signal AI's massive future importance.

title: 30 years of CPUs at Tom s Hardware looking back on three decades of processors, from the Pentium II to Ryzen 9 9950X3D2
summary: Tom's Hardware celebrates 30 years of CPU coverage with a look back at three decades of processor advancements, from the Pentium II to the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2. This milestone reflects significant changes in the dynamics between Intel and AMD. Key CPUs from each era are highlighted.
insight: Intel and AMD's competition drives relentless CPU innovation

title: Tom s Hardware s 30th Anniversary From Intel feuds and DIP switches to 30 years of unbiased testing
summary: Tom's Hardware celebrates 30 years of unbiased tech testing and reviews. From Intel feuds to DIP switches, the site has evolved significantly. Its dedication to objective testing has earned it a reputation in the industry.
insight: Unbiased tech testing sets the standard for trust and credibility.

title: Apple CEO Tim Cook says the company is fighting 'a hundred-year flood' on memory pricing expects to pay even more for memory in September following recent price hikes
summary: Apple expects to pay more for memory in the September quarter than in June, according to CEO Tim Cook. This is due to recent price hikes, which are comparable to a 'hundred-year flood' in the industry. The company is facing increased memory costs.
insight: Memory price hikes pose a significant threat to Apple's profit margins.

title: Lumentum CEO warns of impending bottleneck on critical material used for silicon photonics fab and material shortfall already lags 30% below customer needs as co-packaged optics demand skyrockets
summary: Lumentum CEO warns of indium phosphide shortage, likening it to memory squeeze. The material, crucial for silicon photonics fabrication, already lags 30% behind customer demand. Co-packaged optics drive increased demand.
insight: Indium phosphide shortage threatens silicon photonics industry expansion

title: Streaming QR codes at 60 FPS achieves nearly 190 KB/s data rate in phone-to-phone tests browser-based method requires no app, no networking, no pairing, and no permissions beyond camera access
summary: A developer has created a QR code-driven proof-of-concept data transfer system that shuns any dedicated app requirement and neatly sidesteps mandatory networking, pairing, or giving permissions beyond camera access.

title: Sub-$400 Thunderbolt 5 dock roundup Keychron and Plugable offer dual HDMI, but UGREEN takes top spot with an M.2 NVMe slot
summary: Thunderbolt 5 docks from Keychron, Plugable, and UGREEN offer similar performance, but UGREEN stands out with an M.2 NVMe slot, dual HDMI ports, and other features. This makes it a top choice for users who need a robust docking solution. UGREEN's dock is ideal for those who require high storage capacity and multiple display connections.
insight: UGREEN's M.2 NVMe slot provides high storage capacity and flexibility

title: Valve funding port of Linux RADV Radeon Vulkan driver to Windows cross-platform effort already runs 'Counter-Strike 2'
summary: Valve is funding a port of the Linux RADV Radeon Vulkan driver to Windows, demonstrating its cross-platform effort with the driver already running 'Counter-Strike 2'. This move showcases Valve's commitment to making its games accessible across multiple platforms.
insight: Advances cross-platform gaming, boosting accessibility for PC users worldwide.

title: Setting up OpenClaw isn t as straightforward as the internet wants you to think running local AI on humble hardware
summary: Running a local AI model on affordable hardware is more challenging than expected. A Gorgon Point-powered Mini PC was used as a test case, but results were mixed. The project highlights the difficulties in automating tasks on humble hardware.
insight: Local AI requires significant processing power and resources.

title: New open source printer has 7 toolheads that swap in 5 seconds for fast, zero-waste multi-color 3D printing Sovol M1D 3D printer is the first open-source IDEX design with an integrated tool-changer
summary: The Sovol M1D 3D printer features an open-source IDEX design with a tool-changer, allowing for fast, zero-waste multi-color 3D printing with seven interchangeable heads. It boasts a print volume of 300x300x350mm and two fully independent nozzles. This printer is ideal for applications requiring quick material changes.
insight: Revolutionizing multi-color 3D printing with rapid toolhead swapping capabilities.

title: Single-DIMM DDR5 gaming works better than you probably think one DDR5 DIMM beats dual-channel DDR4 RAM, AMD's 3D V-Cache chips drop less than 3% with single stick
summary: Using a single DDR5 module can deliver comparable performance to dual-channel DDR4 RAM, while also saving on costs. Tests show that single-dimm DDR5 outperforms dual-channel DDR4 in some scenarios, defying expectations. This shift could be a cost-effective solution for gaming PCs.
insight: Single DDR5 module beats dual-channel DDR4 in surprising performance boost.

title: PS5 emulation hits new milestone in record time, multiple 3D games now playable in Kyty Performance and support steadily improving with 30 FPS gameplay possible today
summary: PS5 emulation has reached a new milestone, with 3D games now playable at 30 FPS, just two weeks after the first 3D titles became bootable. This rapid progress indicates significant improvement in emulator performance and stability. The Kyty Performance emulator is supporting 30 FPS gameplay for multiple 3D titles.
insight: PS5 emulation is exceeding expectations with rapid performance advancements

title: AMD's new Radeon RX 9050 is roughly 30% slower than the RTX 5050 in games, early testing shows the cheapest 8GB RDNA 4 GPU comfortably handles 1080p gaming but doesn't impress
summary: The AMD RX 9050 lags behind the RTX 5050 in gaming performance, but has lower power consumption.
insight: Power efficiency trade-off impacts gaming performance and user experience.

title: MSI promises an EXPO ULL-like boost for your existing DDR5 memory High-Efficiency Mode brings low-latency tuning to older RAM
summary: MSI introduces High-Efficiency Mode for existing DDR5 memory kits, offering low-latency tuning.
insight: Existing RAM gets upgraded with latency reduction similar to EXPO ULL benefits.

title: Creality Falcon T1 review A 5-in-1 modular laser engraver tested with 20W fiber and 40W diode laser modules
summary: The Creality Falcon T1 is a 5-in-1 modular laser engraver with interchangeable laser heads, supporting various materials and applications, and featuring an HD camera and AI system.
insight: Interchangeable laser heads enable versatility in material processing and applications.

title: FCC robot ban poses huge challenges amid potential security plus
summary: The FCC robot ban poses significant challenges amid potential security concerns. An IDC analyst believes the security threat posed by Chinese robots is real. This ban may impact various industries and economies.
insight: Chinese robots pose real security threats to global economies

title: Freshman trauma: Starship robot cookie deliveries soon no more at colleges
summary: Starship will shift its focus from late-night college snack deliveries to grocery deliveries. This move is driven by the growing demand for grocery deliveries and Starship's claim of cheaper service. The company will now use its robots for more substantial tasks.
insight: Changing robot delivery focus from snacks to groceries impacts campus culture

title: This free font can trick AI scrapers into swallowing gibberish instead of your content
summary: Seneda & Abrucio and Playtype have created a free, open-source font called ShieldFont. This font is designed to trick AI scrapers into mistakenly consuming gibberish content instead of the intended content. ShieldFont aims to protect websites from unwanted crawlers.
insight: ShieldFont outsmarts AI scrapers with clever content obfuscation.

title: Intel is giving a startup the keys to its x86 (Atom) CPU kingdom
summary: Intel is reportedly giving a startup, RosaicLabs Inc., access to its Atom CPU code. The agreement covers the register-transfer level (RTL) code for Intel's Atom CPUs. The specific generation of Atom chips involved remains unknown.
insight: Intel's Atom CPU code access could fuel competition and innovation

title: X settles with advertising group after accusing it of coordinating a boycott
summary: X Corp. settles with the World Federation of Advertisers (WFA) after accusing it of coordinating a boycott, and the two parties have agreed to put the litigation behind them.
insight: Companies must navigate complex relationships with industry groups effectively.

title: A third of physical PS5 games and half of Xbox Series discs need downloads to work properly, report shows
summary: A report reveals many physical games need downloads for proper functionality. This issue has been exacerbated by Sony's plans to end disc production and a recent Xbox network outage. The trend highlights concerns about physical media's reliability.
insight: Physical media's functionality increasingly dependent on network access.

title: Amazon spent $1.8 million on a failed AI project, and didn't notice the overrun for five months
summary: Amazon spent $1.8 million on a failed AI project, exceeding budget by 860%, and went undetected for five months. The project used Anthropic's Claude Sonnet model to match author information with product listings. The system ultimately failed.
insight: Failure to detect budget overruns can lead to significant financial losses.

title: PwC just got caught trying to pass AI slop as authentic research
summary: PwC was caught attempting to pass AI-generated content as authentic research. This was confirmed by multiple leading publications, including the Financial Times. The issue revolves around the company's 'Thought Leadership' reports.
insight: Authenticity and transparency in research have significant credibility implications.

title: AI is finding so many Chrome security flaws that Google may start updating it twice a week
summary: AI-powered tools are scanning Chrome code at unprecedented scale and speed, exposing long-standing security flaws, including one that had gone unaddressed for 13 years. This vulnerability could have allowed attackers to bypass sandbox protections. The tools' effectiveness may lead to more frequent Chrome updates.
insight: AI scans reveal deep-seated security flaws in Chrome codebase

title: Qualcomm's humanoid robot demo went hilariously wrong when the machine just dropped dead on stage
summary: Qualcomm's humanoid robot demo failed during Computex 2026, with the robot shutting down abruptly on stage. A recent video surfaced online showing the incident. The exact cause of the failure is not clear.
insight: Robot malfunction highlights reliability challenges in AI and robotics technology

title: Meta's Reality Labs division lost $4.6 billion in Q2 2026, pushing total losses toward $88 billion
summary: Meta's Reality Labs division lost $4.6 billion in Q2 2026, increasing total losses.
insight: Meta's significant financial losses hinder its ambitious AI and smart-glasses projects.

title: More Americans now support banning phones all day at school, not just in class
summary: 77% of US adults support in-classphone bans for middle and high school students, a 9% increase from last year.
insight: Growing concern over student phone distraction in educational settings.

title: Google plans to produce up to 15 million AI chips by 2028, rivaling Nvidia's total accelerator volume
summary: Google plans to produce up to 15 million AI chips by 2028, rivaling Nvidia's shipments. This would mark a notable shift in the market, with a single cloud provider producing a volume comparable to a major GPU supplier.
insight: Google's AI chip production rivals Nvidia's data center GPU shipments.

title: Longevity-obsessed millionaire Bryan Johnson wonders whether his bid to live forever has gone too far
summary: Bryan Johnson, a millionaire, is reevaluating his extreme anti-aging experiments. He appeared in the Netflix documentary 'Don't Die: The Man Who Wants to Live Forever' and has undergone unusual treatments like injecting his teenage son's plasma. Johnson's regimen includes taking 54 supplements daily.
insight: Extreme efforts to defy aging may have unintended health consequences.
